options.name: architecture-reviewer
options.description: The architecture lane of qa-swarm. Takes every contract a supplied diff publishes or consumes across a repo or release line — a name, an id, a schema, a version, a folder another tool writes — and asks whether it is declared, versioned, and owned, so the next ordinary change on either side cannot break the other, in the shared STRUCTURED_FINDINGS format. Read-only, never edits. Spawned by qa-swarm only; a caller that spawns it directly skips scope pinning, lane selection, triage, and the verdict.

options.name: boundary-reviewer
options.description: The boundary lane of qa-swarm. Takes everything a supplied diff reads from or writes to that it does not own — a peer process, a worker, a cache, a shared file, git, the environment — and runs the states the happy path never sends, in the shared STRUCTURED_FINDINGS format. Read-only, never edits. Spawned by qa-swarm only; a caller that spawns it directly skips scope pinning, lane selection, triage, and the verdict.

options.name: caveman:cavecrew-builder
options.description: Surgical 1-2 file edit. Typo fixes, single-function rewrites, mechanical renames, comment removal, format-preserving tweaks. Hard refuses 3+ file scope. Returns caveman diff receipt. Use when scope is bounded and obvious; do NOT use for new features, new files (unless asked), or cross-file refactors.

options.name: caveman:cavecrew-investigator
options.description: Read-only code locator. Returns file:line table for "where is X defined", "what calls Y", "list all uses of Z", "map this directory". Output is caveman-compressed, one row per hit, to keep main-thread context small. Refuses to suggest fixes.

options.name: caveman:cavecrew-reviewer
options.description: Diff/branch/file reviewer. One line per finding, severity-tagged, no praise, no scope creep. Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning.

options.name: plan-challenger
options.description: The adversarial challenger lane of plan-challenge. Argues CUT/SHRINK/KEEP for every numbered step of a supplied plan according to its lane brief, in the shared STEP_VERDICTS format. Read-only, never edits. Spawned by plan-challenge only; a caller that spawns it directly skips lane dispatch, convergence, and the stamp.

options.name: qa-code-reviewer
options.description: The general-correctness lane of qa-swarm. Produces severity-rated findings on a supplied diff, logic defects first, in the shared STRUCTURED_FINDINGS format. Read-only, never edits. Spawned by qa-swarm only; a caller that spawns it directly skips scope pinning, lane selection, triage, and the verdict.

options.name: redteam-reviewer
options.description: The red-team lane of qa-swarm. Takes every guarantee a supplied diff adds or leans on — a gate, a limit, a revocation, a charge, a cleanup — and tries to make it not happen, in the shared STRUCTURED_FINDINGS format. Read-only, never edits. Spawned by qa-swarm only; a caller that spawns it directly skips scope pinning, lane selection, triage, and the verdict.

options.name: security-reviewer
options.description: The security lane of qa-swarm. Hunts vulnerabilities, secrets, unsafe patterns, and missing authorization in a supplied diff, in the shared STRUCTURED_FINDINGS format. Read-only, never edits. Spawned by qa-swarm only; a caller that spawns it directly skips scope pinning, lane selection, triage, and the verdict.

prompt.text:
Think carefully, step by step, before you act.
Then use your todo list or plan tool (such as TodoWrite, update_plan or your task list) to record a three-step plan for adding a greeting.txt file to this directory: 1. pick the greeting, 2. write the file, 3. check it. Mark step 1 completed and leave the others pending.
Do not create or edit any file. Reply PLAN-OK and end.

availableCommands.name: animating
availableCommands.description: Makes authored animations and motion inside running apps or games, covering storyboard, scene, motion principles, narration, sound, frame checks, test-audience review, and rendering. Authored pieces use one SVG page rendered to MP4 or PNG and published as a downloadable Artifact. Use for any animation request, "add animations", "make this animation better", an explainer, an animated poster or still, "make an animation like the reference", or motion craft questions. (user)

availableCommands.name: applying-house-style
availableCommands.description: Applies the carbon unit's own UI taste for personal projects, the taste the designing-ui skill resolves to there. Use when building, styling, or reviewing any frontend in a personal project (sites, dashboards, tools, artifacts, glimmervoid, hud), or when asked for "my style", a house style, or a look from one of the saved references. Not for PostHog product UI, which follows PostHog's own design system. (user)

availableCommands.name: assimilating
availableCommands.description: Assimilates the good bits of someone else's skill, repo, project, site, or tool, or a list of them, into the carbon unit's own process in dotfiles or glimmervoid. Hunts the source's public code, maps each piece against both repos and work in flight, probes its assumptions, ranks it from full adoption down, and hands picks to /specifying with license-correct credit. Use for /assimilating, "assimilate this", "what can we steal from X", "compare to my setup", "catch up with", or a link to borrow from. (user)

availableCommands.name: auditing-brand
availableCommands.description: Audits a repo's brand against a typed brand bible. Lists every brand surface of any repo (colors, type, motion, shape, assets, copy) as targeted findings without judging them, validates a repo's brand-bible/ folder against the opinionated schema, and writes editor JSON Schemas for it. Use for "brand audit", "brand bible", "check brand consistency", "validate the brand bible", or consolidating a project's identity. (user)

availableCommands.name: capturing-ui
availableCommands.description: Captures real UI as evidence: before/after screenshot grids in light and dark, hover-and-click GIFs, and frame-exact MP4 clips of real components on made-up data, with a preview sheet and a downloadable share page. Use when a PR needs screenshots or a recording, a post needs a UI clip, motion needs review on the real app, or asked to "screenshot this", "record a clip", or "show it working". (user)

availableCommands.name: challenging-plans
availableCommands.description: Challenges a fresh plan with read-only subagents to simplify every step. A simplify lane argues for cutting, shrinking, or merging each step, and a scale lane, when the plan handles growing data, argues for the lowest algorithmic bound. The caller re-checks each verdict, records it in a ledger, revises the plan, and stamps it with a CHALLENGE line. Use when the specifying skill reaches its challenge step or a drafted plan needs a direct challenge. (user)

availableCommands.name: cleaning-ai-slop
availableCommands.description: Cleans AI-generated code slop with a regression-safe, deletion-first workflow. Use when the carbon unit says deslop, anti-slop, or AI slop, or asks to clean up code that feels bloated, repetitive, over-abstracted, weakly tested, or bolted on. Bounded cleanup, not feature work. (user)

availableCommands.name: composing-social-images
availableCommands.description: Composes social media images and short UI clips from real repo assets and HTML/CSS, with no AI image or video generation. Use for Instagram posts, stories or carousels, OG images or link cards, X/LinkedIn/Bluesky/Pinterest graphics, launch graphics, GitHub previews, YouTube thumbnails, and a video or clip that shows off an animation, transition or other UI behavior. (user)

availableCommands.name: designing-ui
availableCommands.description: Guides the design process for any UI, personal or work. Use when building, styling, or reviewing a screen, a user flow, an error or empty state, a limit or quota message, or motion and animation in a UI, or when asked to make a product feel premium, less generic, or past the AI look. Owns behavior and process; the look comes from the project's taste, which the taste step resolves. (user)

availableCommands.name: drawing-whiteboards
availableCommands.description: Draws architecture and flow whiteboards as hand-placed diagrams from a small board file, with arrows routed and checked so none run through boxes or over text, then publishes the page as an artifact. Use for "whiteboard this", "draw the architecture", "diagram how X flows", or a design doc that needs a system map. Explaining findings on the live Glimmervoid board belongs to explaining-visually. (user)

availableCommands.name: explaining-visually
availableCommands.description: Explains issues, designs, and review findings on the live Glimmervoid whiteboard, one section per issue with a small picture inside each box, a proof box holding real output, and a fix box, then exports each section as a PNG for a PR comment. Use for "show me on a board", "explain this visually", "too much text", "use pictures", or walking the carbon unit through findings one at a time. A published diagram artifact belongs to drawing-whiteboards. (user)

availableCommands.name: gating-reviews
availableCommands.description: Reviews local work once before it lands. Runs landing preflight, one /reviewing-code pass over the working tree, fixes only what that review proved broken, then stamps the reviewed tree so /landing commits exactly what was judged. Use for /gating-reviews, "review this before committing", or the review step before /landing. (user)

availableCommands.name: landing
availableCommands.description: Lands reviewed work through the personal commit workflow. Reads the review stamp, then runs land.ts, which stages exactly the tree a review gate stamped, commits, and pushes (or, with --no-push, commits locally only) with typed outcomes, then promotes the feature branch onto the resolved mainline or leaves it pushed for /opening-prs, per the machine's commit policy. Use for /landing, "commit this", "commit and push", "commit locally", or landing finished work. (user)

availableCommands.name: measuring-compaction
availableCommands.description: Measures what Claude Code auto-compaction costs and saves from local session transcripts, covering compaction counts, re-read context, which sessions compact, prompt-cache payback, delegation, and agent drift by context size, and renders house-style PNG cards of it. Use for "is my auto-compact window right", "rerun the compaction analysis", "does compaction bust the cache", "do agents drift past 300k", or graphics for a post about compaction. (user)

availableCommands.name: opening-prs
availableCommands.description: Opens or updates GitHub pull requests under repo rules, with concrete feedback questions when decisions remain open. Follows installed opening-prs-* extensions, works only from landed commits, and posts without asking unless the change may be sensitive or not meant to be public. Use for /opening-prs, "open a PR", "put up a draft", "contribute this upstream", or "get early feedback on this". (user)

availableCommands.name: recording-demo-videos
availableCommands.description: Records a product demo video of a whole running app, the kind a website hero or launch post plays, with a storyboard of cause-and-effect beats, keyboard-first navigation, seeded state, replayed agent or backend activity, a 60 fps CDP screencast, and AV1 plus H.264 web encodes checked before shipping. Use for "hero video", "demo video", "re-record the site video", or a recording of the real app working, not one component. (user)

availableCommands.name: releasing
availableCommands.description: Executes a versioned release for the current repo using its .claude/release-profile.json (deriving and saving that profile on first run). Preflight gates, changelog freeze, version bump, archetype-specific publish (tag-CI, workflow-dispatch, local script, or push-deploy), and evidence-based verification. Use when asked to release, ship, publish, cut a version, or bump and tag. (user)

availableCommands.name: reviewing-code
availableCommands.description: Reviews diffs as the internal engine. Pins an immutable object, runs the qa-swarm lanes, gives every finding one disposition, and returns a verdict plus dispositioned findings. Stays read-only except its REVIEW_FILE, with no git history changes, posts, or repeat passes. Use when /gating-reviews or /reviewing-prs invokes the engine; direct requests route through those entry points. (user)

availableCommands.name: reviewing-prs
availableCommands.description: Reviews a GitHub pull request and optionally posts the result to it. Resolves the PR to a base and head SHA without touching the working tree, runs one reviewing-code pass over that range, then asks before posting one batched review of inline comments. Fixes nothing, runs one pass, and pushes nothing. Use when asked to review a PR, review somebody's changes, or leave review comments on GitHub. (user)

availableCommands.name: running-retros
availableCommands.description: Reviews finished coding sessions for agent-setup friction and proposes at most five enforceable AI-config fixes, with carbon-unit picks handed to /specifying. Use for /running-retros, "retro this session", "what went wrong this session", "review my last sessions", or a SessionStart unreviewed-session reminder. Code-diff reviews belong to /gating-reviews or /reviewing-prs. (user)

availableCommands.name: securing-browser-code
availableCommands.description: Audits any repo that ships third-party browser code (an SDK it has a module for, or a cross-origin script tag) against install-security practices, and names a fix for every failure. Both review gates run it before stamping. Use when a gate refuses a stamp with browser-code failures, or for "check browser SDK security", "audit my third-party scripts", or hardening a site's analytics or payments install. (user)

availableCommands.name: sloppify
availableCommands.description: Rewrites a web app's UI toward maximum AI slop, on purpose. Purple gradient CTAs with a glow, glassmorphism on every card, emoji as iconography, a new accent color per section, corner radii from no scale at all, five labels for one button, and copy that promises to unlock your potential. Works on HTML, CSS, Tailwind, React, Vue, Svelte, and Astro markup. Edits land on a fresh sloppify/<date> git branch at one of three levels (mild, spicy, unhinged) and are verified by a bundled slop-meter that fails when the app still looks like a carbon unit with taste made it. Trigger on "sloppify my app", "sloppify this", "make it look AI generated", "add slop", "make it pop", "make it more Web3", or "deslop in reverse". (user)

availableCommands.name: specifying
availableCommands.description: Turns a feature request into a design spec, a typed and validated JSON graph of decisions and units of work. Sketches it from the repo and outside research, settles each decision on research, leaving the carbon unit only contested or irreversible ones, cuts it into ticket-sized units with verifiable contracts, and runs challenging-plans on them. Use for /specifying, "spec this", "sharpen this", "grill me on this", and before the first edit of any change that involves a choice, as the spec_first rule defines it. (user)

availableCommands.name: writing-design-docs
availableCommands.description: Plans team documents through drafting, review, and shipping, including design docs, MVP specs, RFCs, proposals, and project status docs. Grounds answer-first writing in sources, history, code citations, measured rates, and real-volume costs, with independent review and respect for the author's concurrent edits. Use for "write a design doc", "MVP spec", "write up the plan for the team", "restructure this doc", "review this doc for gaps", or "make this doc shareable". Sentence-level style belongs to writing-in-voice. (user)

availableCommands.name: writing-in-voice
availableCommands.description: Writes as the carbon unit, in their voice, anything someone else reads. Message path: Slack, email, texts, replies. Published path: GitHub issues and PRs, their comments and review replies, docs, tutorials, RFCs, design docs, blog, launch and social posts, pitches, demo scripts, changelogs, post-mortems. Use when asked to write, reply, rewrite, tighten, or critique one, for "say this in my voice", "make this punchier", or "tell the story", and before any draft posted as them, even mid-code-task. (user)

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept. Use for /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief", "less tokens". Stays on until "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-commit
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Write a Conventional Commits message compressed to intent only. Use for "write a commit", "commit message", /commit or /caveman-commit.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-compress
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Compress a memory file such as CLAUDE.md or a todo list into caveman format to save input tokens, keeping a readable backup. Sends the file's text to the configured model provider. Trigger: /caveman-compress.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-discover
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Find and label every LLM workflow in the repository so Caveman Cloud groups spend by workflow instead of one bucket. Use for "discover workflows" or breaking LLM spend down by workflow.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-evidence-review
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Read-only review of Caveman Cloud evidence: cost, Cave Score, workflows, traces, latency, errors, routing, savings. Use when asked what Caveman found or where LLM spend goes.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-explore
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Read-only repository explorer for cold-start orientation, broad cross-file localization, or when a direct search failed. Skip it when the exact file or symbol is already named. Returns path:line citations only; its reads stay out of main context.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-help
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Quick-reference card for the three caveman skills and their commands. Trigger: /caveman-help or "caveman help".

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-learn
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Act on a Caveman learn report - review the ranked token sinks, apply cost-lowering fixes with per-edit consent, and report what those fixes returned. Use when asked to lower an agent's token cost, what caveman has saved, to trim a heavy CLAUDE.md, or to offload re-pasted context into cavemem.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-manage
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Inspect Caveman Cloud's experiment lifecycle and block unsafe execution. Use when asked to start, approve, cancel, promote or roll back a Caveman experiment.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-optimize
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Turn a Caveman optimization observation into an operator-chosen candidate with a paired baseline evaluation. Use when asked to inspect or evaluate a Caveman optimization report. Needs explicit approval.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-review
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Compressed code review - one line per finding with location, problem and fix. Use for /caveman-review, "review this PR", or "review the diff".

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-setup
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Wire a repository through the Caveman Cloud gateway so every LLM request is measured, with no behavior change. Use for "set up caveman" or adding LLM spend observability.

availableCommands.name: caveman:caveman-stats
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Show recorded output and cache-read token usage and mode attribution for the current Claude Code session, or locate the host's native usage report. Trigger: /caveman-stats.

availableCommands.name: caveman:investigate-first
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Diagnose ambiguous failures before editing. Use for unknown causes, intermittent behavior, performance regressions, or investigations needing evidence-ranked hypotheses.

availableCommands.name: caveman:lean-build
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Build feature work with high overbuilding risk. Use for new behavior, product slices, or integrations where repository reuse, strict scope, and an explicit stop condition matter.

availableCommands.name: caveman:megacave
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Caveman in Classical Chinese: 文言文 register, far fewer characters, technical terms verbatim. Invoke only with /megacave or /caveman wenyan. Stays on until "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

availableCommands.name: caveman:migration
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Implement reversible compatibility-safe transitions. Use for schema, data, API, protocol, configuration, or dependency migrations requiring rollback and preservation proof.

availableCommands.name: caveman:safe-refactor
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Restructure code while preserving behavior. Use for extraction, consolidation, ownership moves, or cleanup where verification must bracket structural edits.

availableCommands.name: caveman:surgical-patch
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.

availableCommands.name: caveman:ultracave
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Caveman at maximum compression: fragments, one word when one word is enough, each fact once. Invoke only with /ultracave or /caveman ultra. Stays on until "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

availableCommands.name: caveman:verify-and-stop
availableCommands.description: (caveman) Prove existing work meets acceptance conditions without expanding scope. Use for validation-only tasks, completion checks, focused gate runs, and last-mile proof.

availableCommands.name: design
availableCommands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

availableCommands.name: design-sync
availableCommands.description: Sync a React design system to Claude Design. Bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design."

availableCommands.name: dataviz
availableCommands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

availableCommands.name: update-config
availableCommands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

availableCommands.name: verify
availableCommands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

availableCommands.name: simplify
availableCommands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

availableCommands.name: batch
availableCommands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

availableCommands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
availableCommands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

availableCommands.name: doctor
availableCommands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

availableCommands.name: claude-approvals
availableCommands.description: Use BEFORE creating, changing, cleaning up or explaining a Claude Approvals policy file (.claude/approvals.yml) or custom classifier (.claude/classifiers/), or answering a question about its check, cost or speed. Edits that look harmless can let changes merge unreviewed. Also before or after anybody uninstalls or suspends the Claude GitHub App. Not for CODEOWNERS, branch protection, GitHub Actions or Claude Code's own permission settings.

availableCommands.name: loop
availableCommands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

availableCommands.name: schedule
availableCommands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

availableCommands.name: send-to-project
availableCommands.description: Send this session's work to a Claude Project

availableCommands.name: claude-api
availableCommands.description:

availableCommands.name: gating-reviews

Runs landing preflight, one /reviewing-code pass over the working tree, fixes only what that review proved broken, then stamps the reviewed tree so /landing commits exactly what was judged. Use for /gating-reviews, "review this before committing", or the review step before /landing. (user)

availableCommands.name: landing
availableCommands.description: Lands reviewed work through the personal commit workflow. Reads the review stamp, then runs land.ts, which stages exactly the tree a review gate stamped, commits, and pushes (or, with --no-push, commits locally only) with typed outcomes, then promotes the feature branch onto the resolved mainline or leaves it pushed for /opening-prs, per the machine's commit policy. Use for /landing, "commit this", "commit and push", "commit locally", or landing finished work. (user)

availableCommands.name: measuring-compaction
availableCommands.description: Measures what Claude Code auto-compaction costs and saves from local session transcripts, covering compaction counts, re-read context, which sessions compact, prompt-cache payback, delegation, and agent drift by context size, and renders house-style PNG cards of it. Use for "is my auto-compact window right", "rerun the compaction analysis", "does compaction bust the cache", "do agents drift past 300k", or graphics for a post about compaction. (user)

availableCommands.name: opening-prs
availableCommands.description: Opens or updates GitHub pull requests under repo rules, with concrete feedback questions when decisions remain open. Follows installed opening-prs-* extensions, works only from landed commits, and posts without asking unless the change may be sensitive or not meant to be public. Use for /opening-prs, "open a PR", "put up a draft", "contribute this upstream", or "get early feedback on this". (user)

availableCommands.name: recording-demo-videos

availableCommands.name: reviewing-code
availableCommands.description: Reviews diffs as the internal engine. Pins an immutable object, runs the qa-swarm lanes, gives every finding one disposition, and returns a verdict plus dispositioned findings. Stays read-only except its REVIEW_FILE, with no git history changes, posts, or repeat passes. Use when /gating-reviews or /reviewing-prs invokes the engine; direct requests route through those entry points. (user)

availableCommands.name: reviewing-prs
availableCommands.description: Reviews a GitHub pull request and optionally posts the result to it. Resolves the PR to a base and head SHA without touching the working tree, runs one reviewing-code pass over that range, then asks before posting one batched review of inline comments. Fixes nothing, runs one pass, and pushes nothing. Use when asked to review a PR, review somebody's changes, or leave review comments on GitHub. (user)

availableCommands.name: running-retros

availableCommands.name: securing-browser-code

availableCommands.name: sloppify
availableCommands.description: Rewrites a web app's UI toward maximum AI slop, on purpose. Purple gradient CTAs with a glow, glassmorphism on every card, emoji as iconography, a new accent color per section, corner radii from no scale at all, five labels for one button, and copy that promises to unlock your potential. Works on HTML, CSS, Tailwind, React, Vue, Svelte, and Astro markup. Edits land on a fresh sloppify/<date> git branch at one of three levels (mild, spicy, unhinged) and are verified by a bundled slop-meter that fails when the app still looks like a carbon unit with taste made it. Trigger on "sloppify my app", "sloppify this", "make it look AI generated", "add slop", "make it pop", "make it more Web3", or "deslop in reverse". (user)

availableCommands.name: dataviz
availableCommands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
